reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster, primarily because it directly addresses the key demands of trail running – climbing strength and trail-specific power – through a significant focus on hill workouts. Furthermore, the inclusion of a longer, controlled long run (90 minutes) after the hill work helps consolidate the gains made. While Plan B has a slightly longer overall duration, it doesn't prioritize the specific adaptations needed for trail running speed and efficiency.
